BiblicalUsage: The word means to waver or slip, and the psalms use it for feet that hold firm and feet that would fall. David says God enlarged his steps under him so his feet did not slip, and he prays that his steps would hold fast in God's paths. Job says the wavering foot is despised by those at ease, and the psalm of the man who trusts God says the law of God is in his heart and none of his steps shall slide.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the wavering foot is the picture of every believer's weakness, and God does not ask us to stand on our own strength. I hold that He enlarges our steps beneath us, so the one who walks with Him does not slip, even on ground that would make others fall.
